Strike · Romania

Drone strike sets YARA J on fire near Sulina; crew safe

14 October 2026 · YARA J near Sulina · Drone strike and fire

Drone strike confirmed by Romania’s president; Russian origin assessed by a NATO military source

A drone struck the Comoros-flagged tanker YARA J near Sulina on 14 October 2026. Romania’s president confirmed the attack the next day. A NATO military source cited by Reuters assessed the drones that hit YARA J and WINE TRADER as Russian in origin; a specific operator has not been established in the reviewed reporting.

The crew reported an explosion and fire. The fire was extinguished and all reported 17 crew were safe, with no injuries or sinking reported. The vessel was inside Romanian territorial waters. MRCC requested assistance at 20:25; SAR Apollo departed at 20:31 and was recalled at 21:30 after the crew said help was no longer needed. These are rescue times, not a verified strike time.

This updates the original incident and retains its URL. The initial absence of a radar-detected approach does not undo the later attack confirmation. A connection to the 20:04 radar episode in N085 remains unproven. WINE TRADER and Sea Destiny have separate records.

Attribution and uncertainty

Origin / operator / attribution
Russian-origin drones, according to a NATO military source cited by Reuters. Romania’s president confirmed the drone attacks on YARA J and WINE TRADER but did not establish state responsibility. The NATO source’s origin assessment is prominent; the specific operator and model are not established in the reviewed reporting.
Investigation / uncertainty
The later presidential confirmation supersedes the initial uncertainty about drone causation. Russian origin is attributed to the NATO military source; a specific operator, model and approach track remain unestablished. The relationship to N085’s lost radar contact remains unknown.

Event categories
Aerial-drone strike on merchant shipping; reported onboard explosion; fire extinguished
What was reported
The crew reported a drone hit, explosion and onboard fire on 14 October. On 15 October Romania’s president confirmed drone strikes on this tanker and WINE TRADER. Reuters cited a NATO military source assessing the attacking drones as Russian in origin.
Aircraft / vessel / quantity
YARA J, a Comoros-flagged chemical/products tanker, reportedly with 17 crew aboard. Aerial drone strike confirmed by the Romanian president; drone number and model unconfirmed.
Origin / operator / attribution
Russian-origin drones, according to a NATO military source cited by Reuters. Romania’s president confirmed the drone attacks on YARA J and WINE TRADER but did not establish state responsibility. The NATO source’s origin assessment is prominent; the specific operator and model are not established in the reviewed reporting.
Damage / casualties / disruption
Fire extinguished; all reported 17 crew safe, with no injuries reported. Extent of structural damage not established; no sinking reported.
Response / outcome
MRCC requested assistance at 20:25. SAR Apollo departed at 20:31 and was recalled at 21:30 after the crew reported the fire out and no assistance needed.
Investigation / uncertainty
The later presidential confirmation supersedes the initial uncertainty about drone causation. Russian origin is attributed to the NATO military source; a specific operator, model and approach track remain unestablished. The relationship to N085’s lost radar contact remains unknown.
Route / entry mechanism
Vessel was anchored and in ballast near Sulina. No verified drone approach track. The minister initially said radar had not detected an approaching drone; later reporting confirms the attack without supplying a track.
Explosive payload
Weapon and payload not identified. An onboard explosion was reported by the crew and described at the superstructure in the defence minister’s later account.
Counting / links
One ship-incident record combining strike, reported blast, fire and response. Updates N086 in place, preserving its date, ID and URL. Cross-reference N085’s 20:04 radar episode; no shared target is established. WINE TRADER (N090) and Sea Destiny (N089) are separate vessel incidents.
